Circle Farming
The most common and most effective way to farm is to pick a route and run in a circle. this way the mobs you killed at the beginning of your route have had
time to respawn and you can run in an infinite loop until you have gathered 10 monstrous essences and have to return back to town to collect your bestiary reward
You dont have to return to town to go to the blacksmith when your inventory is full if you have a familiar with the "Salvager" Trait
Dont forget to select "auto pickup loot" in the settings, otherwise your farming experience will be miserable.
Group Farming
Farming in the same Zone with a party of four has a few benefits:
the legendary drop chance is increased.
you have a chance of random normal gem drops (12 per day).
you will farm much faster because you work together when killing monsters
you will gain more experience, because you can keep kill streaks going which will reward you with bonus EXP.
Tagging
The first player who lands an attack on a monster "tags" the monster and gets all the rewards when it dies.
if another player has tagged a monster you will see its Name "whitened" instead of e.g. blue/yellow/red
If the player who has tagged the monster dies while attacking it, another player can tag it
Monstrous Essences & Beastiary
Monsters in the open world zones randomly drop monstrous essences (about every 2 minutes). Once you have collected 10 of them go to the nearest safe zone
and open your bestiary to collect the rewards. the first turn-in each day gives you a guaranteed legendary item, the first three turn-ins have a random chance of
discovering a new beastiary page. if you already have discovered the page, you get compensated with 3000-6000 gold.
You can turn in monstrous essences more than 3 times a day and you will still get the rewards. Chances of getting legendary items as areward are pretty high here.
Hidden Lairs
Hidden lairs will appear randomly on in the zones you are farming in. they have fixed spots but are not always open.
when a lair opens, you will be notified and guided to the entrance. you can run a lair solo or in a group

The monster difficulty in a Hidden Lair is different then the difficulty in the open world zone. It is the same as in dungeons, so you might have a harder time killing Elites (especially yellow elites).
Running a lair in a group of 4 rewards you with 2 extra chests at the end of each level
Lairs have 2 levels. during each level there are 2 objectives and 1 lair guardian that will drop bonus chests as rewards.
these chests contain normal gems and equipment pieces. if you run in a group of 4 you will get 2 bonus chests at the end of each level.
Hidden Lairs reward guaranteed Normal Gems for each objective (until weekly cap is reached)

Purple Elites
Purple Elites pop up when the "wanted" task occurs. They have fixed spots on the map and always spawn at the same location.
They typically have multiple health bars, symbolized by the red diamonds to the right of the bar
They do moderate damage, but have extremely high health (1,02 Mio).
Killing purple Elites is a good way of gaining dust, so picking a farming spot with multiple purple elite spawn locations is a good choice
Orange Elites
Orange or "Ancient" Elites are a single tough enemy surrounded by 4-6 minions. They are the least common Elite in the game.
They have three random affixes. Their minions all have the Empowered Minion affix which increases Life, Damage, and Movement Speed
The first Orange Elite you kill each day rewards you with a guaranteed legendary item.
The next Orange Elites you kill also have a high legendary drop chance
Yellow Elites
A yellow Elite is a single tough enemy. They are less common than Blue Elites, with two random affixes.
The first 4 yellow Elites each day have a higher chance of dropping a legendary item.
When they die, they drop 3 EXP Globes.
Blue Elites
A blue Elite Pack is always made up of three enemies. They are the most common Elite in the game. Each enemy has the same, singular affix
When they die, they drop 3 EXP Globes.
Normal Mobs
Normal Mobs, or "Trash Mobs" are the most common mobs. They come in different forms and shapes and do vary in HP and Attacking Power
Mobs from Category A do normally drop 1 equipment piece (90%), the Mobs from Category A and B can also drop equipment pieces but they have lower chances

Bounties
Core Gameplay:

Bounties are a fundamental daily activity in Diablo Immortal that involve completing short, localized tasks across various zones of Sanctuary. Players accept these tasks from the Bounty Board in Westmarch
and then travel to the designated areas to fulfill the objectives, which typically involve defeating specific monsters, collecting items, or interacting with certain objects.
Upon completion, players return to the Bounty Board to claim their rewards.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Daily Availability: A set number of 8 Bounties become available each day, resetting at a specific server time.
Save Bounties: You dont have to complete all 8 bounties each day. You can save up to 32 bounties. So if you (like me) want to only do Hellslayer Bounties, just dont do bounties on Saturday and Sunday
and on Monday you will have saved up 24 bounties and you can do them all in 6 Hellslayer Runs.
Varied Objectives: Bounty objectives are diverse and can include:
Monster Slaying: Defeating a specific number of a particular type of monster in a designated zone.
Elite Hunting: Defeating a named elite monster or a group of elites with specific affixes.
Item Collection: Gathering a certain number of items dropped by specific enemies or found in the environment.
Zone Specific: Each Bounty will direct the player to a particular zone within Sanctuary, encouraging exploration of different areas.
Easy to Pick Up and Complete: Bounties are generally designed to be relatively quick and straightforward to complete, making them a good daily activity for players with limited playtime.
Rewards:
Chance for Gear: While not the primary reward, there is always a chance for monsters defeated during Bounties to drop Legendary items, based on the player's Magic Find and the game's drop rates.
Bonus Chest Rewards: The daily bonus chest for completing all Bounties often contains additional Gold, Experience, and sometimes other useful items or crafting materials.

Challenge Dungeons
Challenge Dungeons are harder to complete but offer far more rewards than normal dungeons. Each week you will get a guaranteed Green Set for completing your first Challenge Dungeon.
Monsters have 300% more life and deal 200% more damage
Boss Monsters have a chance to be "Ancient Bosses" that drop an additional Plunder Chest which contains a Green Set Item

Challenge Dungeons have up to 2 modifiers which can be negative or positive
Negative
Big Problem: Enemies are larger throughout the dungeon. The player's size is decreased. Bosses will continuously grow over time until they enrage.
Laser: Enemies fire beams of energy at targets.
Bad Blood: Enemies may leave behind a pool of blood after death that will slow and damage players.
Bolstered: Some non-Boss monsters have an aura that increased movement and attack speed of nearby monsters, and gives them a shield.
Rain of Fire: Fireballs occasionally fall from the sky, leaving burning areas that will damage the player.
Sacrificial Power: Skills have greatly reduced cooldowns but cost Health.
Lava Eruption: Lava periodically erupts beneath the player.
Conjurer: Some monsters and Bosses summon doppelgangers.

Electric: Players will periodically be marked with Positive or Negative. Standing close to players with the same status will reduce cooldowns; standing close to players with the opposite status will damage both players.
Explosive Reaction: Enemies will periodically be marked. After a short delay, marked enemies will explode. All enemies hit by the explosion will become explode.
Chains: Up to two players will periodically be chained together. The chained players take continuous damage until they run away from each other to break the chain.
Neutral
Swarming: The dungeon has more normal monsters throughout.
S-Class: The dungeon has more elite monsters throughout.
Gauntlet: The dungeon has no normal monsters, and Bosses are stronger.
Heightened Senses: Monsters sense players more easily and have greatly increased movement speed.
Positive
Speed Run: Completing the dungeon within the time limit will grant bonus rewards.
Bountiful: Combat Globes drop more frequently.
Greed's Spoils: Skip directly to the final Dungeon Boss. The Boss’s difficulty is increased.
Disruptive Portal: A portal will appear at a random point within the dungeon, releasing an extremely powerful enemy. Defeat the enemy to earn an extra reward.
Erratic Assault: Similar to Greed’s Spoils, skip directly to the final dungeon boss and continue through up to 3 additional Erratic Assault Portals to face additional bosses.

Castle Erebban
Castle Erebban is a game mode in Diablo Immortal that was introduced alongside Abyssal Verge in the "Age of Unmaking" update.
It offers a different kind of challenge compared to surviving the encroaching darkness of the Verge.
Gameplay and Objectives:
Escape the Castle: The primary goal in Castle Erebban is to escape the perilous castle. You start at one end and must navigate through its randomly generated corridors and rooms to reach the exit.
Increase Danger Level: As you explore the castle, you'll encounter and defeat demons. Defeating these enemies increases your "Danger Level," represented by a meter.
Reaching certain Danger Levels unlocks more rewarding chests within the castle. There are a total of 8 Danger Levels.

Loot Chests: Scattered throughout Castle Erebban are chests that become available as you increase your Danger Level. These chests contain various rewards. Reaching Danger Level 6 spawns the final, most valuable chest.

The Boss - Araban: Once you reach Danger Level 8 or linger for too long, a powerful boss named Araban will begin to hunt you and the primary objective shifts to escaping the castle while being pursued.

Limited Time (Soft): While there isn't a strict timer, the appearance of Araban acts as a soft time limit, encouraging players to loot efficiently and make their way towards the exit before becoming overwhelmed.
Solo or Party: Castle Erebban can be played solo or with a party.

Accursed Towers
While fighting demonic hordes for control of the tower, a clan’s objective is to collect Cursed Shards from slain demons.
To deal damage to their foes, players need to locate and activate the tower’s Curse Sources. Doing so will make enemies vulnerable, allowing players to dispatch them and collect their Cursed Shards.
Once the timer runs out, the top 10 clan members with the highest Cursed Shard amounts will have them added to their team’s total.
A clan can choose to do as many runs to collect Cursed Shards at the same tower as they desire, but only the highest team total will be retained.
If a clan has collected the most Cursed Shards among all clans vying for that specific tower by Saturday at 7 p.m. server time, then their clan will claim the tower.
Even after taking the tower, Hell will attempt to retake it. Once the Corruption meter reaches a certain amount, demonic incursions will follow.
Members of the clan must come to defend their tower promptly or else it will be lost and can be reclaimed by another clan.
The demons can be warded off by powering up the tower. Within the Accursed Tower's menu, the clan leader can choose to power up their tower.
Doing so will not only end the attacks on it from demons but increase the bonuses provided by the tower and periodic rewards provided by the rewards chest inside of it.
However, if the tower is powered up, other clans will be able to challenge the owning clan for control of the tower through PvP
Gameplay
You can run the Accursed Towers Solo or in a group of 4.

Terror Rifts
Core Gameplay:

Players enter a temporary, localized area within a designated zone of Sanctuary through a Terror Portal. Inside, the primary gameplay loop involves defeating challenging monsters to collect Stygian Fragments.
These fragments are then used to activate Stygian Spires scattered throughout the area. Activating a spire immediately summons a powerful boss that players must defeat to earn a reward chest.
The goal is to efficiently farm fragments and activate up to four spires and defeat their corresponding bosses within the limited duration of the Terror Rift instance.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Always Available, Single Zone: Terror Rifts are no longer time-gated and appear in one random zone across Sanctuary at any given time. The active zone is indicated on the world map.
Terror Portals: These portals spawn periodically within the active zone and serve as the entry point to a Terror Rift instance.
Stygian Fragments: These are the primary currency earned by defeating monsters within a Terror Rift instance. They are required to activate Stygian Spires.
Stygian Spires: Interactable objects within the Terror Rift instance. Activating them consumes Stygian Fragments (increasing cost per activation) and immediately summons a boss.
Boss Encounters: Each activated spire summons a boss that players must defeat.
Limited Instance Duration: Each Terror Rift instance lasts for a limited time (approximately 13 minutes). Players must complete their activities within this timeframe.

Solo or Party Play: Players can participate in Terror Rifts solo or in parties. Fragment collection and spire activation are generally individual efforts, though parties of 4 can have the benefit of collecting normal gems along the way
Rewards:
Reward Chests: Defeating a boss summoned by a Stygian Spire grants a reward chest. Players can earn up to four chests per Terror Rift instance.

Eternal Equipment: These chests have a chance to contain Eternal Equipment, a powerful gear type with three primary attributes and four magic affixes. This is the primary incentive for participating in Terror Rifts.

Terror Essence: Defeating bosses and completing Terror Rifts also rewards Terror Essence, a currency used to interact with Oblivion Pillars/Helliquary Bounties for additional rewards, including more Eternal Equipment.
Weekly Reward Limit: Players can earn a maximum of 10 Terror Rift reward chests per week.
Oblivion Pillars
Core Gameplay:
Oblivion Pillars are an endgame activity in Diablo Immortal that become accessible after participating in Terror Rifts and accumulating Terror Essence.
Players interact with these pillars to initiate challenging combat encounters against waves of powerful enemies and a final boss within a confined area.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Terror Essence Cost: Interacting with an Oblivion Pillar requires using 1 Terror Essence, which is primarily obtained by completing Terror Rifts
Instanced Encounters: Activating an Oblivion Pillar transports the player (and their party, if applicable) to a private, instanced area.

Wave-Based Combat: Within the instance, players face multiple waves of increasingly challenging monsters. These waves often include a mix of standard enemies, elites with affixes, and potentially unique enemy types.
Final Boss Encounter: After successfully clearing all the waves, a powerful final boss will spawn. This boss typically has unique mechanics and abilities that players need to learn and counter.
Limited Attempts: If you run 50(?) Oblivion Pillars in a week, the difficulty of the mob & boss encounter rises significantly
Rewards:
Eternal Equipment: The primary reward for successfully completing an Oblivion Pillar encounter is the chance of dropping a piece of Eternal Equipment.
Hellslayer Bounty
Core Gameplay:

Hellslayer Bounties offer players a more efficient way to complete their daily Bounties. By spending Terror Essence, earned from participating in Terror Rifts, players can condense four regular Bounties

into a single, more challenging Hellslayer Bounty. Completing this single bounty provides rewards equivalent to or greater than completing four individual Bounties, often with the chance of obtaining valuable Eternal Equipment.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Consumes Terror Essence: Activating a Hellslayer Bounty requires spending Terror Essence. The exact cost might vary but is typically one Terror Essence to convert four regular Bounties.

Replaces Four Regular Bounties: Upon activation, a Hellslayer Bounty replaces four of your available regular Bounty slots for the day. It counts as completing four Bounties for daily and Battle Pass progression.
Faster Completion (Potentially): While more challenging, a single Hellslayer Bounty can often be completed faster than traveling to and completing four separate regular Bounties.

Access through Bounty Board: Players can access the option to convert regular Bounties into a Hellslayer Bounty at the Bounty Board in Westmarch. There is a button to "Upgrade" Bounties using Terror Essence.
Daily Availability: The number of Hellslayer Bounties a player can do per day is limited by their Terror Essence availability and the number of regular Bounties they are willing to convert.
Rewards:
Equivalent to Four Regular Bounties: Players receive the standard rewards for completing four regular Bounties (Gold, Experience, Battle Pass Points).

Chance for Eternal Equipment: A significant advantage of Hellslayer Bounties is the chance to receive Eternal Equipment upon completion. This is the same powerful gear type with triple primary attributes
and four magic affixes that can also be obtained from Oblivion Pillars. The drop rate might vary.
Vanguard
Core Gameplay:
Vanguard is a cooperative PvE game mode designed for four players. You access it through a portal in Deckard Cain's Workshop (unlocked at Hell I difficulty)
Like Helliquary Raids, Vanguard is available twice a week (Mon / Thu). The first 5 completions after the weekly resets get you the maximum rewards
Key Features and Mechanics:
Vanguard Charms: This is a unique mechanic of the Vanguard mode. By participating, you earn Vanguard Charms. These charms provide powerful temporary buffs to your party within the Vanguard instance.
There are four categories of Vanguard skills (Might, Defense, Heal, Bane), with two skills in each.
You start with basic versions of these skills.
By successfully completing Vanguard runs, you earn experience to upgrade your Vanguard skills, making them more potent for future runs. These upgrades are persistent.
Vanguard skills include:
Might: Increasing Critical Hit Chance or adding piercing attacks to primary attacks.
Defense: Granting shields or selflessly taking damage for allies.
Heal: Conjuring healing fields or tracking orbs.
Bane: Dealing area damage and reducing enemy attack/movement speed or increasing damage enemies take.
Difficulty Levels: Vanguard has multiple difficulty levels (likely Normal, Hell, and potentially higher "Elite" tiers). Higher difficulties feature tougher enemies, bosses with more mechanics,
and may require higher-level Vanguard Charms to succeed.
Leaderboard: There is a leaderboard for Vanguard Elite Clears
Helliquary Affixes: Completing Vanguard runs on higher difficulty tiers can reward you with special Helliquary Affixes. These affixes, once acquired, can be used anywhere in Sanctuary and
enhance your Primary Attacks in unique ways (e.g., triggering boss skills on primary attacks).
Rewards:
Vanguard Charms: As mentioned, these are earned through participation and are essential for progressing in the mode.
Equipment: You receive standard equipment drops (including a chance for set items and Legendary items) for defeating enemies and bosses within Vanguard.
Helliquary Affixes: These powerful account-wide bonuses are a significant incentive for tackling higher Vanguard difficulties.
Helliquary Raid
Helliquary Raids are challenging boss encounters that can be undertaken solo or cooperatively with a raid party of up to eight players.
The difficulty (HP of the Boss) scales (more players = more HP), and the rewards adjust based on the number of participants, emphasizing both individual skill and group coordination.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Boss-Specific Mechanics: Each Helliquary boss has its own set of unique attacks, phases, and environmental hazards. Understanding these mechanics is crucial for survival and dealing effective damage.
Weekly Reset: Rewards for defeating each Helliquary boss are typically limited to twice per week per difficulty level.
Difficulty Scaling: Helliquary bosses become progressively more challenging in higher difficulties, requiring higher Combat Rating and better coordination.

Helliquary Progression Link: Defeating Helliquary bosses is essential for progressing your Helliquary, a system that unlocks permanent stat bonuses and powerful Demonic Remains to further enhance your character.
Unlock Difficulties: Defeating the last Helliquary Boss of each difficulty unlocks the next higher difficulty (together with reaching the required Paragon Level)
Rewards:
Twice a week: Players can typically receive rewards for defeating each Helliquary boss 5 times twice per week (resetting on Mondays and Thursdays).

The first completion of a Helliquary Raid grants a Bonus EXP Reward of 2.000.000 which is not subject to the EXP Penalty, so it is often used if you want to push Paragon Levels before a new difficulty
Voucher: If you do the Raids with your Warband you get a Voucher for an Eternal legendary Crest (1xweek) - you still have to buy it for 1600 HILT though

Scoria/Voidblood Slag: Defeating Helliquary bosses is a primary source of Scoria (for Normal/Hell difficulties) and Voidblood Slag (for Inferno difficulties). These materials are used to upgrade your Helliquary.
Demonic Remains: Each Helliquary boss drops specific Demonic Remains. These unique items can be slotted into your upgraded Helliquary to grant significant and often build-defining passive bonuses.
Key Strategies:
Know the Boss Mechanics: Before engaging a new Helliquary boss, research its abilities and phases through guides or by observing experienced players. Understanding what to expect is paramount.

Strategic Positioning: Proper positioning is required to avoid deadly boss attacks and maximize damage output. Spread out to avoid area-of-effect damage or stack in specific locations for buffs or healing
High DPS: Bring your highest DPS build or Support build for your damage dealers
Helliquary Gauntlet
Core Gameplay:
The Helliquary Gauntlet is a game mode in Diablo Immortal that allows players to test their speed and skill against a sequence of Helliquary bosses.
Success in the Gauntlet often rewards players with a spot on server-wide leaderboards, offering prestige and small rewards
The Gauntlet involves facing a fixed order of Helliquary bosses. The faster you can defeat each boss, the better your overall time. Efficiency in combat and understanding boss mechanics are crucial.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Time-Based Challenge: The primary objective is to defeat a predetermined sequence of Helliquary bosses as quickly as possible. Your final clear time determines your ranking on the leaderboards.
Solo or Group: Unlike Helliquary Raids, the difficulty (HP) of the bosses does not scales with the number of participants, so it is significantly harder to clear them solo or in small groups.
Server Leaderboards: A central feature of the Helliquary Gauntlet is the competitive aspect introduced by server-wide leaderboards.

Repeatable for Leaderboard Ranking: While the most substantial gear rewards for the first clear of each Gauntlet tier, players can run the Gauntlet repeatedly to improve their clear times and achieve a higher ranking
on the server leaderboards. Subsequent clears might offer lesser rewards like crafting materials or gold.
Seasonal Nature: The Helliquary Gauntlet has a seasonal aspect, with leaderboards resetting and new tiers or boss sequences being introduced with major game updates.
Rewards:

First-Clear Rewards: Completing a tier of the Helliquary Gauntlet for the first time grants significant rewards (2 triple stat Set Items + 2 triple Stat Primary Gear Pieces) as well as Demonic Remains and 2.000.000 EXP
which is not subject to the EXP Penalty and is often used when pushing Paragon Levels (do Gauntlet last when pushing to get your triple stats items already with the new difficulty stats)

Cosmetic Rewards: In the past, achieving certain milestones or first clears in the Helliquary Gauntlet has also awarded unique cosmetic items, such as weapon or armor skins, providing a visual indicator of your accomplishment.

Timed Challenges: Each floor presents a time limit within which all enemies must be defeated to progress to the next. Failing to clear a floor within the time limit requires repeating it.

Hilts: Significant amounts of Hilts are awarded for reaching certain milestone floors (e.g., every 5 or 10 floors). Hilts are a valuable currency used to purchase various items, including Legendary items and Crests.

Alley of Blood
Key Features and Mechanics:
When the Cycle of Strife gets into the Gathering Phase, Shadow Clans compete against each other in Shadow War Battles.
The Diablo Immortal Shadow War is split into tournament-style brackets consisting of two playoff rounds between opposing clans.
In order to decide which clans face off against each other, the groups in each bracket are split into three ranks, A through C.
Initially, your clan’s rank in the Shadow War will match its rank within the Shadows faction, but this will change based on your clan’s victories and losses in subsequent battles.
Clans will compete in 2 matches per week, earning points for each match that they win. Moving away from a traditional bracket, this means that there will be no eliminations,
and Clans will be matched against other Clans with similar points totals. Clans will earn 3 points for a win, and 1 point for a loss.
The top ten Clans with the highest scores at the end of the tournament will be greatly rewarded, with Clans that finish from 11-20 earning hearty rewards as well.
Registration: Registration for the Shadow War begins each week on Monday, 3 a.m.—Tuesday, 9 p.m. local server time. Each Clan will need 30 players to register.
If you meet the requirements, you’ll register automatically but can switch back to manual registration if wanted.
Matchmaking Rules: If two Clans have already faced off against each other in the previous round, you’re far less likely to play against them in the following rounds.
Clans that are ranked in the top 10 are placed in a protected matchmaking pool. When there’s multiple potential opponents with similar point totals, the matchmaking system will prioritize
matching you against opponents ranked 11 or lower, whoever's points are closest.
Rewards: The top 10 Clans will earn Legendary Crests for each members, while the following Clans who finish 11—20 will earn a Legendary Crest Voucher which allows you to purchase a Legendary Crest
from the Hilts Trader until 9 p.m. local server time the following Saturday.
The event starts at 7:30 p.m. server time on Thursdays for the Preliminary Round and 7:30 p.m. server time on Saturdays for the Final and Third Place Playoff Rounds.
The countdown to the Shadow War's beginning will start at 7:30 p.m. server time. You have 10min to prepare
The feature decides the top ten dark clans that go on to the Cycle of Strife.
Rewards: Players that engage in the Shadow War are rewarded with experience and a guaranteed random Legendary item (you get this in the mail - keep it for paragon pushes)
Vigil of Blades
Core Gameplay:
Vigil of Blades is a weekly PvP event that takes place during the first three weeks of a new Immortal reign. It pits the top Shadow Clans against the Immortals in a series of 8v8 matches.
The faction that wins the majority of these matches gains a significant damage and health buff that will aid them in the upcoming Rite of Exile.
The Battle itself works like the Alley of Blood Limited-Time-Event
Alley of Blood
Key Features and Mechanics:
Weekly Event (Early Immortal Reign): This event occurs once per week, specifically during the initial phase of a new Immortal reign (weeks 1, 2, and 3).
Top Shadow Clans vs. Immortals: The 3 highest-ranking Shadow Clans (by Ranking on Tuesday evening) participate against teams formed by the current Immortal faction.
Series of 8v8 Matches: The event consists of multiple 8v8 matches between the participating Shadow and Immortal teams.
Point-Based Scoring: Winning matches awards points to the respective faction. There are 4 rows with 3 Matches in each row.
Matches in the first row award 8 points, second raw 4 points, third row 2 points and fourth row 1 point. So there is a total of 3x(8+4+2+1) = 45 Points. Whoever gets 23 Points or more wins.
In order to win the Vigil of Blades a faction needs to win 2 battles out of the 3.
Buff for Rite of Exile: The primary purpose of Vigil of Blades is to determine which faction (Shadows or Immortals) will receive a significant damage and health buff for the Rite of Exile
that follows in later weeks. The faction that accumulates the most points by winning matches gains this advantage.
The Buff for each won battle is +4%, so a total of +12% damage and life buff is possible if a faction manages to win all 3 weeks - which is a huge advantage
Spectator Mode and Predictions: All players on the server can spectate the Vigil of Blades matches. There's also a prediction system where players can bet on which faction they believe will win,
earning HILT rewards for correct predictions.
Rewards:

Damage and Health Buff for Rite of Exile: The winning faction (Shadows or Immortals) gains a valuable +4% damage and health buff that will be active for their participants in the subsequent Rite of Exile.
This is the primary reward and significantly impacts the outcome of the final battle for control.
Rewards for Participants: Players participating in the Vigil of Blades receive Rewards in the Mail similar to Shadow Wars
Rewards for Correct Predictions: Players who correctly predict the winning faction in the Vigil of Blades receive HILT rewards
Rite of Exile
The culmination of the Cycle of Strife, the Diablo Immortal Rite of Exile sees the top ten Dark Clans face off against the Diablo Immortal Immortals faction.
The Dark Clans use this opportunity to try and overthrow the server’s reigning clan and become the new Immortals.
The Rite of Exile always takes place on Sundays at 8pm server time in the 4th week of the Immortal reign
There are three stages to the Rite of Exile (below)
If the Shadows lose during any stage of the Rite of Exile, the reign of the current Immortals continues, forcing the Shadows to try again the following week.
The Rite of Exile can be attempted 4 times until the Shadows, inevitably, win in week 7.
Rite of Exile (First Phase)
The initial Rite of Exile phase sees the top ten Dark Clans each send their eight best fighters into an 8v8 battle against eight Immortals, for a total of ten simultaneous 8v8 fights.
These fights take place on the standard battlegrounds map, and involve sub-objectives such as escorting statues to new locations, and destroying key objectives on the map.
In Week 4, Shadows need to win 6 out of 10 matches to get to the Second Phase
In Week 5, Shadows need to win 5 out of 10 matches to get to the Second Phase
In Week 6, Shadows need to win 4 out of 10 matches to get to the Second Phase
In Week 7 the Immortal Reign will be over BUT if Shadows win 4 out of 10 matches , the Immortals cannot achieve a "blessed reign"
Immortals: The Immortals should focus on getting at least 6 good teams together and match them against the weakest Shadow Clans to win the overall fights
Shadows: Each Clan should bring their strongest team to have the best chances
Challenge of the Immortal (Second Phase)
All participating Shadow Clan Leaders have to choose 2 Clan Members to fight alongside them in a large-scale 30vs1 battle against the Immortal Leader, known as Challenge of the Immortal.
The Immortal is transformed into a powerful raid boss with special abilities, and the Shadows need to defeat the Immortal before the time runs out or a death cap is reached.
If the Shadows win, they enter the final phase.
Strategy:  No real strategy here, just try to kill as many Shadows as possible. Most likely the Shadows will win this fight
Shadows: Since this fight will most likely be won you should already focus on the final battle. Try not to get your Gladiator/Savior procced and look for a
nice place to "hide" in any of the corners, along or in close proximity to allied clans.
Ranged Classes are at an advantage here because the Immortal has mostly melee attacks
The Final Battle ( Third Phase)
After the Immortal is beaten, all 30 players are immediately resurrected and fight in a battle royale against each other,
and the winner claims the Eternal Crown. The leader of the Dark Clan the winner belongs to then becomes the new Immortal,
and their clan also forms the core of the Immortals faction going into the new Cycle of Strife.
Once the latest iteration of the Immortals has been assembled, the current Cycle of Strife officially ends and a new one begins.
This process automatically disbands every other Dark Clan, and the Shadows players that didn’t join the new Immortals faction become
adventurers once again.

Shadows: Try to stay out of fights as long as possible. Stay together, try to avoid "friendly fire" with allied clans and try to take advantage of players that are vulnerable after fighting other players

Having a clear strategy for this fight is crucial because although there will be allied clans fighting in this battle, all players except for your own clan members are considered enemies on the plattform,
so auto-attacks, AoE Damage or aggressive pets will eventually hit your allies - be careful and fight smart
You need a significant distance from enemies to use the bandage for healing, so always communicate and make sure there is a safe space to heal for retreating allies
Classes with high survivability are at an advantage here (Barbarians, Necromancer, Tempest, Monk)

A Blessed Reign is the ultimate achievement for the Immortal faction, signifying a full seven weeks of successful defense against the

Kion's Ordeal
Core Gameplay:

Kion's Ordeal is a cooperative, large-scale raid available exclusively to members of the Immortal faction. Led by the Immortal Leader or Lieutenants, up to 48 Immortals participate in a coordinated effort to defeat

four powerful Tormentors (bosses) within a limited time. The core gameplay involves splitting into smaller groups to engage each boss simultaneously, strategically managing their health to defeat them close together,
and ultimately earning rewards and a powerful buff for the Immortal reign.

After the Tormentors have been killed all participants have a chance of winning extra legendary items by standing in circles for 4 rounds of an "item lottery". The circles indicate what kind of gear you could be winning.
Points are awarded randomly, whoever gets the most out of the people standing in the same circle (between 0 and 102) wins the item

it's generally one pick per Immortal across all four rounds (thats how most clans do it). This means if you are lucky enough to be selected in the first round, you won't get another pick in subsequent rounds.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Large-Scale Cooperative Raid (Up to 48 Players): A significant number of Immortals can participate in a single run, emphasizing the strength and unity of the ruling faction.
Four Boss Encounters (Tormentors): The raid features four distinct bosses that must be defeated. These bosses have their own unique abilities and attack patterns.
Simultaneous Engagement: The raid is designed for multiple groups of Immortals to engage each of the four bosses concurrently.
Strategic Boss Health Management: A key mechanic is to bring all four bosses to low health at roughly the same time and then defeat them in quick succession.
Defeating bosses too far apart in time will enrage the remaining bosses, making them significantly more difficult (this aspect is no longer relevant - Kion should be easy to complete)
Multiple Difficulty Levels: Kion's Ordeal has multiple difficulty levels, offering greater challenges and potentially better rewards for stronger Immortal factions.
Rewards:
Blessing of Daedessa: By completing Kion's Ordeal, the Immortals gain Daedassas Blessing, which allows them to earn 3 Aspirant Keys for completing 3 Elder Rifts each day
Dominance: Completing the raid grants a significant amount of Dominance, contributing to the Immortal reign's overall strength and potentially unlocking cosmetic rewards.
Legendary Crest: The first completion of Kion in the week grants you am unbound Legendary Crest
Aspirant Keys: Kion awards 15 Aspirant Keys
Key Strategies:
Bring your highest DPS build or Support-Buff Build to finish the Tormentors quickly

Alley of Blood
This is a unique and engaging PvP (Player vs. Player) game mode in Diablo Immortal that offers a more structured and team-based experience compared to the open-world PvP zones.
The PVP map is used for Shadow War and Vigil of Blades as well as for the limited-time-event "Alley of Blood"
The limited-time variant equalizes all players strength and only uses 6 Primary Gear Slots.
Gameplay and Objectives:
Team-Based PvP: Alley of Blood pits two teams of eight players against each other in a lane-style arena
Guardians: An AI-controlled Guardian pushes forward for each team. Destroying him and letting your own guardian attack enemy towers is a key to victory
Towers: Each team has 2 towers defending each team's base. Sentry Towers defend themselves and deal damage to Guardians in their proximity first, then the player.
Champion's Marks: Defeating enemy heroes, super minions, and towers drops special "badges" or "Champion's Marks." Collecting these marks strengthens your character,
making you harder to defeat and increasing your damage output. You can have a maximum of 99 Champion’s Marks, with each one increasing your power and character’s size.
Resurrection Mechanics: Upon death, players are automatically resurrected after a short period. The resurrection time typically increases as the match progresses.
Movement Speed Boost: Players start the match with a temporary 5s boost to movement speed to facilitate early engagement.
Destroy Ancient Heart The primary objective is to destroy the Ancient Heart in the opposite Side of the Alley
Limited Match Time: Matches have a time limit. If neither team reaches the victory point threshold before the time expires, the team with the higher score wins.
Healing Wells / Bandage: There are respawning Wells that drop 3 Health Potions at strategic locations on the map. The bandage has a 60-second cooldown.
Special Skills: Before a match begins, players will pick one of the below Specialist skills to add to an additional Skill slot.
Teams can’t have more than two players per Skills category, but those players can select the same sub-Skill.

Conqueror / Tower Wars

This is a recurring limited-time PvP event as well as the PVP map to defend Clan Towers in Diablo Immortal that offers a more strategic and territory control-focused experience compared to the standard Battlegrounds.
Gameplay and Objectives:
Limited-Time Event: Conqueror is a recurring limited-time PvP event, so it's not always available. 1 Keep an eye on in-game announcements to know when it's active.
Large-Scale Territory Control (Usually 10v10 or similar): Conqueror typically involves two teams of players battling to control key strategic points across a larger map than the Battleground arenas.

Capture and Hold Towers: The primary objective is to capture and hold multiple Control Towers scattered throughout the map. These towers function as capture points, similar to flags in other territory control games.
Accumulate Points: Teams earn points continuously for each Control Tower they control. The more towers a team holds, the faster their point total increases.
Number of Towers
First to Reach the Score Limit: The first team to reach a predetermined score limit of 1300 wins the match.
Contesting Towers: To capture an enemy-controlled tower, you need to be within its vicinity without any enemy players present. The capture process takes a certain amount of time.
The more allies present, the faster the tower is captured. Enemy players within the capture radius will halt the process.
Defending Towers: Once a tower is captured, you need to defend it from being retaken by the enemy team.
Strategic Map Movement: Effective movement across the larger map is crucial for capturing undefended towers, reinforcing contested ones, and cutting off enemy advances.
Respawning: Defeated players will respawn after a short delay, allowing them to rejoin the fight and contribute to their team's efforts. Respawns happen in waves every 25s
Limited Match Time: Matches have a time limit to prevent them from becoming too drawn out. The team with the higher score at the end of the time limit wins if neither team reaches the score limit.
Guardian Spawn: When a team reaches 1000 Points, a Guardian between the middle and the closer outer tower spawns. The team who defeats him gets 200 points
The Map:
Larger and More Open: Conqueror maps are typically larger and more open than Battleground arenas, allowing for more strategic movement and flanking maneuvers.
Multiple Control Points: The maps feature several strategically placed Control Towers that teams will fight over.
Key Strategies:

Teamwork and Coordination: Effective communication and coordination are vital for capturing and holding multiple towers simultaneously. Designate players to attack specific towers or defend key locations.
Map Awareness: Understanding the layout of the map, the locations of the Control Towers, and the movement of enemy players is crucial for strategic decision-making.
Tower Prioritization: Decide which towers are most important to capture (the middle one!) and hold based on their location and the current flow of the battle.
Balanced Team Composition: Having a mix of different classes with varying roles (damage dealers, tanks, support) can be beneficial for both attacking and defending towers.
Early Aggression: Often, making early pushes to capture undefended towers can give your team a significant point advantage.
Reinforcement and Defense: Once a tower is captured, ensure that enough players remain to defend it from enemy counter-attacks.
Utilize Crowd Control and Support: Skills that can disrupt enemy captures, protect allies, or heal teammates are crucial for controlling towers.
Adapt to Enemy Movements: Pay attention to where the enemy team is focusing their efforts and adjust your strategy accordingly.
Pro Tip: The "Unstuck" button can teleport you to your base (only every 30min, so once a game)
Wild Brawl
Core Gameplay:
Wild Brawl is a limited-time, multi-team Player vs. Player (PvP) arena-style game mode. Typically, four teams of four players (though this can sometimes vary) are dropped into a designated zone

(often a modified section of the Dark Wood). The objective is survival – your team must be the last one standing. The arena space shrinks over time due to encroaching lethal darkness, forcing teams into increasingly

close and dangerous engagements until only one team remains victorious. Players start at a fixed level (usually Level 60 for the event) and progress by gaining experience and looting gear within the match
to strengthen their characters. A key unique element is the temporary acquisition and upgrading of skills from any class upon leveling up during the brawl.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Multi-Team Last Team Standing: Unlike the 1v1 format of Duel or the two-team structure of Battlegrounds, Wild Brawl pits multiple teams against each other in a free-for-all until one survives.
In-Match Leveling and Gear Acquisition: Players begin with basic equipment and level up by defeating monsters (environmental mobs that spawn within the arena) and other players.
Each level gained allows players to choose a new skill or upgrade an existing one. Gear is found in chests scattered throughout the arena and dropped by defeated players and monsters.
Cross-Class Skill Choices: A defining feature of Wild Brawl is that the skills offered upon leveling up are not restricted to your chosen class. You might find powerful abilities from other classes,
leading to highly adaptable and unpredictable character builds within a single match. Up to six skills can be equipped at any time.

Shrinking Playable Area: As the match progresses, a lethal darkness closes in on the arena, reducing the safe zone and forcing teams to confront each other. Staying outside the safe zone results in rapid health depletion.
Environmental Hazards and Features: The arena may contain environmental elements like tall grass for stealth, destructible objects, or specific terrain features that can be used strategically.
Bandage Healing: Instead of standard health potions, players typically have access to a limited-use bandage item with a significant cooldown, emphasizing careful play and tactical retreats.
Key Strategies:
Success in Wild Brawl requires a blend of combat skill, strategic looting, and adaptability:
Early Looting and Leveling: Quickly explore the arena to find chests and defeat early monsters to gain a level and acquire better starting gear.
Strategic Skill Selection: Carefully consider the skill choices offered upon leveling. Look for skills that synergize with your current gear and playstyle, even if they are from an unfamiliar class.
Team Coordination: Stick with your team, communicate effectively, and focus fire on enemy players. Reviving fallen teammates quickly (if the mechanic is active) is crucial.
Awareness of the Shrinking Zone: Constantly monitor the encroaching darkness and reposition your team to stay within the safe area. Getting caught outside the zone is often a death sentence.
Environmental Awareness: Utilize the terrain and any environmental features to your advantage, such as using tall grass for ambushes or line-of-sight breaks.
Bandage Management: Use your bandages wisely and avoid taking unnecessary damage, as healing is limited.
Focus Fire: Coordinate with your team to focus damage on a single enemy player to eliminate them quickly.
Trial of the Hordes
Core Gameplay:
Trial of the Hordes is a Player vs. Player (PvP) event where two individual players (of the same class) compete to see who can defeat more waves of demons within a limited timeframe.

Players not only fight their own hordes but can also strategically spawn additional, tougher demons into their opponent's lane to overwhelm them. The player with the highest score at the end of the trial wins.
Key Features and Mechanics:
1v1 Same-Class PvP: Players are matched against another player using the same class. This emphasizes skill and build optimization within the constraints of a specific class.
Wave-Based Demon Slaying: Both players face continuous waves of demons spawning in their respective lanes. The difficulty and types of demons increase over time.
Orb Collection and Enemy Spawning: Defeating certain enemies drops orbs. These orbs are crucial as they allow players to spawn additional, challenging demons into their opponent's lane
Limited Time Matches: Each Trial of the Hordes match has a set time limit. The player with the highest cumulative score (based on the number and type of demons defeated) at the end of the time wins.
Ranking System and Leaderboards: The event features a ranking system where players gain or lose points based on their wins and losses.
Rewards:
Reward Chest: The reward chest offering you a gear piece (of the difficulty your are in when opening the chest) is the best part about the mode.
If you are constantly losing and wonder why please watch Craines Video "how to always win in Trial of the Hordes"
Sentinel's Stand
Core Gameplay:
Sentinel's Stand is a recurring daily solo event located in the Southern Dreadlands zone. Players must strategically defend a central Shardstorm (the Sentinel) against waves of demons that attack
from multiple paths. The core gameplay involves collecting resources dropped by defeated enemies to build and upgrade defensive towers around the Shardstorm to prevent the demons from reaching it.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Daily Solo Event: Players can participate in Sentinel's Stand once per day. The event becomes available at a specific time and remains active for a certain duration.
Location: Southern Dreadlands: The event takes place within a specific area of the Southern Dreadlands zone, indicated on the map when active.

Tower Defense: Players utilize a tower defense system, strategically placing and upgrading various types of towers with different attack styles and elemental affinities to combat the incoming demonic hordes.
Wave-Based Attacks: Demons attack in 5 waves, approaching the Shardstorm from different directions. The number and strength of enemies increase with each wave.
Resource Management: Defeating enemies grants a resource that is used to build and upgrade towers. Efficient resource management is crucial for establishing a strong defense.

Tower Variety: Players can build different types of towers, such as those that deal single-target damage, area-of-effect damage, apply crowd control (like slowing or freezing), or exploit enemy weaknesses (indicated during the waves).
Tower Upgrades: Towers can be upgraded 4 times to increase their damage output, attack speed and range
Limited Tower Slots: There is a limit of 10 towers a player can build simultaneously, requiring strategic placement and decisions on which towers to prioritize.
Victory Condition: Victory is achieved by successfully defending the Shardstorm against all waves of demons before they can destroy it.
Rewards:
Bonus Chests: Completing the event with a high success rate rewards you with a guaranteed legendary item

After completing the event, your towers will continue to slay enemies for 60min. After that a notification will pop up and you can return to the Event to collect all loot (might include 1-3 more legendaries)
Key Strategies:
Early Resource Prioritization: Focus on building 3 Boltcasters in the first lane, upgrade 2 of them to level 2. Then keep building/upgrading Boltcasters
Elemental Advantage: Pay attention to any elemental weaknesses the incoming demon waves might have. Build towers with corresponding elemental damage to deal increased damage.
Fractured Plane
Fractured Plane is a unique and engaging game mode in Diablo Immortal that offers a refreshing departure from the usual grind.
Gameplay and Objectives:
Limited-Time Event: The Fractured Plane is a recurring limited-time event, meaning it's not always available. When it is active, it offers a distinct gameplay experience.
Start with Nothing: Unlike other game modes yYou begin with a basic class template, no gear, and a set of temporary skills.
9 Floors of Challenges: The Fractured Plane consists of 9 randomly generated floors, each presenting a unique set of challenges.
Acquire Temporary Gear and Powers: As you progress through the floors, you'll find temporary gear, gems, and powerful Blessings.
Temporary Gear: This gear is specific to the Fractured Plane run and provides stats and sometimes unique effects. You'll constantly be finding and replacing gear as you go.
Temporary Gems: Similar to regular gems but only for the duration of the run, these enhance your stats.

Blessings: These are powerful, run-specific buffs that can significantly impact your character's abilities and playstyle. You earn Blessings by completing certain challenges or finding them within the floors.
These can range from increased damage to unique skill modifications.

Adapt and Build: The core of the Fractured Plane lies in adapting to the gear and Blessings you find. You'll need to make strategic decisions about which items to equip and how to utilize your temporary
skills in combination with your acquired powers.
No Paragon Levels or Existing Gear: Your character's Paragon level, existing gear, and gems have no impact within the Fractured Plane.
It's a test of your understanding of your class mechanics and your ability to make the most of what you find.
Rewards:
You can get a lot of Legendary items (4+) for each completion of The Fractured Planes
Key Strategies:
Understand Your Class Mechanics: Even though you start with basic skills, a solid understanding of your chosen class's core mechanics and potential skill synergies will be beneficial.
Prioritize Survivability: Since too many deaths means restarting, focusing on staying alive is crucial. Don't be afraid to play defensively if necessary.
Survivor's Bane
Core Gameplay:
Survivor's Bane is a top-down survival mode where you must defend against endlessly spawning enemies while collecting the experience orbs they drop to earn new skills.
Eventually elite monsters and bosses will spawn that drop equipment. The character automatically uses all of its available skills so you only need to control the movement.

Each run of Survivor's Bane resets the character progress, and you must re-earn all the skills and equipment. Every level up presents a random choice of skills which could be a new skill or an upgrade
to an existing one. Elite monsters drop Skill Orbs that also offer a skill choice. The final upgrade of each skill is a choice between two different effects. Rare Elite monsters and bosses drop
Equipment upgrades, which are initially new pieces, then upgrades to existing ones. The character has 6 slots for skills and 6 slots for equipment, once the limits are reached,
new pickups will only be upgrades. If all skills are maxed out, further level-ups and elite group kills will instead drop some coins and scrap materials to be used in the regular Diablo Immortal game
(this seems to have a cap of 15 drops, which can be reached in endless mode with both modifiers active). However after equipment is maxed out, further item upgrade drops will do nothing.
At one point, a horde of Treasure Goblins can appear, challenging the player to kill as many as possible before they can teleport away, and rewarding lots of equipment in the main game.
Healing Pools spawn around the map and are the most common form of healing. Treasure chests may also spawn containing scrap materials and gold.
Other randomly spawning objects are Conduit Shrines which let you strike nearby enemies with lightning, and Disintegration Shrines which create 5 very powerful beams in front of you that can
cut through masses of enemies or take down a Boss quickly.
The game can be paused, and in fact pausing is automatic while on the skill/equipment upgrade screens.
There are 3 levels, with the bottom two being unlocked by beating the one above them.

Ashwold Cemetery
Endless - is not actually endless. It goes through 4 stages switching randomly between Frozen Tundra, Shassar Sea and Ashwold Cemetery. In the last stage,
bosses appear along with regular monsters (as opposed to despawning them) and eventually the final boss (the Butcher) appears.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Gearless Start: Players begin each Survivor's Bane run without any of their equipped items, emphasizing skill and adaptability.
Random Starting Skill: You'll start with one random skill from your chosen class, forcing you to build from a fresh foundation.
Leveling and Skill Selection within the Run: Defeating enemies grants experience orbs, leading to rapid level-ups. Each level gained offers a choice between equipping a new skill
(potentially from any class) or upgrading an existing one (up to a maximum of six equipped skills).
Elite Monsters and Bosses: Tougher elite monsters and zone-ending bosses with unique abilities will challenge your temporary build.
Automatic Skill Casting: Once you equip skills during a run, they are often cast automatically as you move and encounter enemies, focusing the gameplay on movement, positioning, and skill selection.
Top-Down Perspective: The game mode often shifts to a top-down, vertically scrolling perspective, providing a wider view of incoming threats.
Skills:
Skills are not restricted to your character's class, skills from all classes may show up randomly. The starting skill is based on your class

Key Strategies:
Success in Survivor's Bane relies on quick decision-making and adapting to the available skills:
Prioritize Early Levels and Skills: Focus on quickly gaining a few levels and selecting skills that provide good initial clear speed and survivability.
Synergize Skills: Look for skills that work well together, regardless of their original class. Experiment with different combinations to find powerful synergies.
Adapt to Available Choices: You won't always get your ideal skills. Be prepared to make the best of what's offered and adjust your playstyle accordingly.
Focus on Survival: Since you start without gear, prioritize skills and upgrades that enhance your survivability, such as healing, shields, or crowd control.
Learn Enemy Patterns: Pay attention to the attack patterns of different enemies and bosses to avoid taking unnecessary damage.
Strategic Movement: While skills are often auto-cast, your movement is crucial for dodging attacks and positioning yourself effectively against groups of enemies.
Optimize for AoE and Single-Target: Balance your skill selections to handle both large waves of weaker enemies and tougher single targets like elites and bosses.
Utilize Environmental Features: If present, use any environmental obstacles or features to your advantage.

Ancient Arena
Core Gameplay:

Ancient Arena is a limited-time Player vs. Player (PvP) zone event that takes place in a specific area of Bilefen. It is a free-for-all deathmatch where individual players or small impromptu groups battle

to be the last one standing. The primary objective is to survive the chaotic PvP environment and ultimately open the Nephalem Cache located in the center of the arena to claim its guaranteed Legendary reward.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Free-for-All PvP: All players within the designated Ancient Arena zone are hostile to each other. There are no dedicated teams.
Last Player Standing: The event continues until only one player remains alive within the arena.
Nephalem Cache: A special chest spawns in the center of the arena. The last player(s) alive typically need to interact with and open this chest to complete the event and receive the main reward.
Respawning Restrictions: Once defeated within the Ancient Arena, players are usually unable to respawn or re-enter the event area until it concludes.
Time-Limited Availability: Ancient Arena is not a permanent game mode and appears as a limited-time event
Rewards:
The primary reward for winning the Ancient Arena is a guaranteed Legendary item from the Nephalem Cache. Additional rewards can include:
Key Strategies:
Survival in the Ancient Arena requires a mix of combat skill, situational awareness, and opportunistic play:
Group Up (Early): While it's a free-for-all, forming temporary alliances with other players can significantly increase your chances of survival against solo opponents or larger groups.
Focus Fire: If you are in a group, coordinate your attacks to quickly eliminate individual threats.
Prioritize Survival: Your primary goal is to be the last one standing. Sometimes retreating or avoiding a fight is the best strategy.
Coordinate to Open the Chest: If you are in a group that has survived, work together to ensure someone can safely interact with and open the Nephalem Cache.
Destruction's Call
Core Gameplay:
Destruction's Call is a daily open-world PvP event that takes place within the Ancient's Cradle. Two teams of players engage in a battle to capture and hold flags scattered throughout the zone.

The primary objective is to accumulate points by controlling these flags for a set duration. Players also engage in PvP combat to defend their captured flags and attempt to take control of enemy flags.
Key Features and Mechanics:
Zone-Specific Event: The event occurs within the designated Ancient's Cradle zone.
Timed Event: Destruction's Call has a specific start and end time, occurring periodically.
Capture the Flag: The core mechanic involves capturing neutral flags or taking control of enemy-held flags by standing near them for a period.
Point Accumulation: Teams earn points over time for each flag they control. The first team to reach a target score wins the match.
PvP Combat: Engaging and defeating enemy players is essential for controlling flags and preventing the opposing team from scoring.
Respawning: Players are typically able to respawn after being defeated, allowing for continuous engagement in the battle.
Team-Based Gameplay: Cooperation and coordination within your team are crucial for effectively capturing and defending flags.
Key Strategies:
Flag Prioritization: Identify key flags to capture and defend based on their location and potential to contribute to your score.
Area Control: Work with your team to control strategic areas around flags to prevent enemy capture attempts.
Effective PvP: Engage enemy players to disrupt their flag captures and eliminate threats to your controlled zones.
Utilize Class Strengths: Different classes excel in different roles (e.g., high damage for offense, crowd control for defense). Coordinate your team composition accordingly.
